name: Joshua

facts.author: Joshua, the son of Nun, who led Israel after Moses. The book says that Joshua wrote words in the book of the law of God (24:26). The account of his death at the end was added by others, traditionally Eleazar and Phinehas the priests.
facts.audience: The people of Israel settling in the land of Canaan

about: Joshua continues the story straight after the death of Moses. God tells Joshua to be strong and courageous, to keep His law day and night, and promises to be with him wherever he goes (1:8-9). The spies are hidden by Rahab in Jericho, the river Jordan stops flowing so that the people cross on dry ground, and the walls of Jericho fall down.

After Achan's sin brings defeat at Ai, Israel deals with it and wins. Joshua then defeats the kings of the south and the north, and the book lists thirty-one kings he overcame (12:24). The second half divides the land among the twelve tribes, sets apart cities of refuge and gives towns to the Levites.

The book shows that God kept every good promise He had made to Israel (21:45). In his old age Joshua gathers the people at Shechem and calls them to serve the LORD alone, saying that he and his house will serve the LORD (24:15).

themes.title: God keeps His promises
themes.text: The land promised to Abraham is given to his descendants, just as God said.

themes.title: Courage through God's presence
themes.text: Joshua can be strong because the LORD is with him, as He was with Moses.

themes.title: Obedience brings victory
themes.text: Israel wins when it trusts and obeys God, as at Jericho, and loses when it sins, as at Ai.

themes.title: Choosing to serve the LORD
themes.text: Each generation must decide for itself to put away other gods and serve the LORD faithfully.
